cards.explanation: The answer is the whole earth, east to west. Asaph says God summons the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets. That stretches from one horizon to the other, friends. No corner of the map is left out of that reach. When the Mighty One calls, it's a big call.

The answer is False. Asaph says, "Our God approaches and will not be silent!" He also says consuming fire goes before Him, and a tempest rages around Him. Nothing quiet about that arrival, friends. I've never seen a bakery door open with that much fire and wind, and I hope I never do.

God calls in the heavens and the earth so He can judge His people. Asaph says God summons them "…that He may judge His people…" The call has a purpose, friends, and the text tells us what it is. God is the Judge, and His people are the ones He judges.

The call says the saints should be gathered to Him. It says, “Gather to Me My saints, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.” Gathered to Him, friends. Not scattered, not sent off somewhere. Close to Him.

The answer is True. Asaph says, "And the heavens proclaim His righteousness, for God Himself is Judge." The heavens are doing the announcing, friends. Then the psalm says Selah, right there in the song.

The answer is False. God says, "I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings are ever before Me." They're not in trouble over the offerings, friends. It's like a boss saying, "Your work is fine," and then pulling up a chair for a different talk.

God doesn't need their animals because every beast of the forest is His. He says, "…for every beast of the forest is Mine…" and the cattle on a thousand hills are His too. That's His reason for having no need for a bull from their stall or goats from their pens (Psalm 50:9). The whole forest and a thousand hills of cattle are already His, friends.
The word is world. God says, "If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and the fullness thereof." The whole world, and everything in it. He's not short on anything, friends.

The offering God asks for is a thank offering. He says, "Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High." He owns everything, so what He asks for is thanks. And I'll tell you, friends, thanks is a gift I never get tired of getting.
The word is deliver. God says, "Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me." Day of trouble, call on Him, and He delivers. Simple as that, friends.

God says the wicked hate His instruction. He says, "For you hate My instruction and cast My words behind you." They can say the words and still not want them. Knowing the lines and loving the Lord are two different things, friends.
The answer is True. God says, "When you see a thief, you befriend him, and throw in your lot with adulterers." The wicked don't turn away from a thief, friends. They pull up a chair next to him.

The wicked slander their own brother. God says, "You sit and malign your brother; you slander your own mother’s son." The one being slandered is their brother, their mother's son. Slandering a stranger is bad enough, friends, and this one is family.

God says they thought He was just like them. He says, "You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you." They thought He was the same as they were. I bet that thought felt comfortable for a while, friends. Then comes, "But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face."
The answer is False. God says, "You have done these things, and I kept silent… But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face." The quiet part is over, friends. He's talking now, face to face.
The word is honors. God says, "He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me…" That's a lovely line, friends. Thanks given to God honors Him.

God will show the one who rightly orders his way the salvation of God. He says, "…to him who rightly orders his way, I will show the salvation of God." After all that heavy warning, the psalm ends with a promise. And it's the best one on the list, friends.
